candidates.change_summary: Replace the require(_s) with require(false) so the call always reverts after the external call.
Delete the require(_s) statement so that unsuccessful external calls do not revert and the function completes successfully.
Replace require(_s) with require(!_s) so the function reverts only when the external call succeeds, inverting the success condition.
Change the require condition from `_s` to `!_s`, so the function reverts exactly when the callee call succeeds.
Replace the callee call data `_data` with empty bytes, so the call succeeds without executing the requested calldata.
Replace the low-level call expression in forward with a call to a nonexistent selector, so the external call itself reverts and forward fails the require.
Replace the required success check with one that requires call failure, so a successful callee call reverts and a reverting callee call completes.
Delete the success require, making forward complete even when the callee call fails.

Replace the low-level call with a transfer of zero value to the callee, which succeeds only for payability but does not execute calldata and can fail for non-payable contracts or out-of-gas cases depending on callee fallback behavior.
Remove the require on the low-level call success flag, so failed calls no longer revert the forward function.
Remove the require(_s) check, allowing forward to complete even when the callee call fails.
Invert the success check, requiring the callee call to fail instead of succeed.
Replace the require(_s) guard with an unconditional revert, so forward now always reverts while the original completes when the callee call succeeds.
Delete the require(_s) statement, so forward no longer reverts when the callee call fails, making the original revert and the mutant complete.
Change the call target from the `callee` parameter to `msg.sender`, so the forwarded call goes to the caller instead.
Negate the success requirement by requiring the call to fail instead of succeed.
Replace the require(_s) success check with an inverted failure check, so the function reverts exactly when the external call succeeds and completes when it fails.
